Mariborski vodovod is a regional public utility company responsible for supplying safe and healthy drinking water to the Municipality of Maribor and 15 surrounding municipalities in northeastern Slovenia. In addition to water supply, the company is also responsible for the operation and management of the Central Wastewater Treatment Plant Maribor, ensuring environmentally responsible and sustainable wastewater treatment for the wider region. With more than a century of tradition and extensive professional expertise, the company operates the largest water distribution network in Slovenia, managing 1.723 kilometers of pipelines and over 260 facilities. Each year, it supplies approximately 14 million cubic meters of drinking water to more than 160.000 residents.
The company’s vision is to be a modern, efficient, responsible, and innovative public utility that delivers top-quality services to its users, partners, and owners. Its core mission focuses on the long-term reliability of water sources, infrastructure, and service quality.
To improve efficiency and sustainability, Mariborski vodovod emphasizes the reduction of water losses, which currently stand at approximately 29%, with an Infrastructure Leakage Index (ILI) of 3.4, highlighting potential for further improvement. The water network is divided into 138 District Metered Areas (DMAs), enabling localized flow monitoring, faster leak detection, and targeted interventions.
Technologically advanced and innovation-driven, the company employs modern IT systems, including enterprise resource planning (ERP), geographic information systems (GIS), and SCADA industrial systems. It takes pride in its use of smart technologies, having installed 99.8% of smart meters, enabling accurate billing based on real consumption. Around 260 control meters and sensors throughout the network provide continuous monitoring, while the integration of GIS with a business intelligence (BI) system supports effective management through detailed dashboards and analytics.
Corporate social responsibility is embedded in the company’s operations, encouraging all employees, from staff to leadership, to contribute to sustainable and socially responsible strategies. Mariborski vodovod continuously invests in system modernization, reduces water and energy losses, promotes innovation, and builds a motivated, highly skilled workforce. Through efficient, rational business practices and a process-based organization, the company ensures long-term financial stability while maintaining a strong focus on customer satisfaction, high-quality service, and open, responsive communication.

SOLEIL is one of France'sTrès Grandes Infrastructures de Recherche (TGIR)(Very Large Scale Research Infrastructures), i.e. tools with unique features required for high-level research activities, open to any scientific community wishing to use them, and accessible on the basis of project excellence.
As an ultra-high-tech facility, SOLEIL is at once a platform open to all academic and industrial communities, a cutting-edge, multidisciplinary research laboratory, and a place for general public to share scientific culture. SOLEIL, located at the heart of the Paris-Saclay science cluster, is a civil company* jointly founded by CNRS and CEA.
More concretely, SOLEIL produces synchrotron radiation, an extremely bright light that can be used to explore inert or biological matter down to the atomic scale, thanks to particle accelerators (electrons). The light produced covers a wide range of wavelengths (from infrared to X-rays) and is used in experimental facilities known as “beamlines”.
SOLEIL's missions are, as described in the company's charter:

- To build and operate a synchrotron radiation source and associated experimental facilities

- To conduct research programs using this synchrotron radiation, and to develop its applications

- Make its facilities available to interested national, European, and international scientific communities, and encourage their use by them

- Collaborate and exchange with other synchrotron facilities.

The synchrotron SOLEIL, a unique tool for both academic research and industrial applications, opened to the scientific community in 2008. It is used every year by several thousand researchers from France and abroad, across a wide range of disciplines including physics, biology, chemistry, astrophysics, the environment, and earth sciences. These users are welcomed and accompanied on the beamlines by SOLEIL's scientific and technical teams.

entityDescription:
NAPOP AS is a Norwegian technology company developing circular and symbiotic energy value chains based on hydrogen. Its core competence lies in integrating renewable energy, advanced electrolysis, and smart energy management with industrial and aquaculture processes to achieve resource-efficient, zero-emission operation. The company designs and delivers fuel-cell-based generator systems for mobile and stationary power generation, as well as catalytic hydrogen combustion units (NAPOP IP) for waterborne and airborne heating and industrial steam. These systems serve the construction, infrastructure, and process industries, where low-carbon, flexible, and reliable off-grid energy is essential. NAPOP also delivers hydrogen infrastructure solutions, including storage, transport, pressure management, and safety compliance, enabling full-lifecycle hydrogen utilization.
NAPOP has co-founded DRIV Hydrogen AS (50 % ownership), which produces hydrogen through reforming of biomethanol. Pilot production started in September 2025, with commercial operation planned for December 2025. DRIV Hydrogen supplies Umoe Advanced Composites and Hexagon Purus—two of Europe’s leading Type IV hydrogen-tank manufacturers—with services such as initial filling, testing, and maintenance of hydrogen storage systems.
NAPOP’s patented Integrated Symbiotic Industrial Park (ISI-P) concept couples local renewable-energy generation (solar, wind, or hydro) with electrolysis and land-based recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). A shared energy- and data-management platform reuses surplus heat and oxygen from electrolysis as inputs to fish farming, while dynamic grid connection and local storage enable the provision of grid-balancing services such as frequency and voltage control. The concept achieves up to 40 % local energy self-sufficiency, improving resource utilization, reducing grid dependency, and enhancing energy security. The first ISI-P facility is under development at Åkrestrømmen, Rendalen, where NAPOP owns land and holds aquaculture licences; a second site is planned in Krødsherad. Patent protection was granted on 7 July 2025, and the ISI-P concept is designed as a replicable, integrated industrial module deployable nationally and internationally.
NAPOP wholly owns VIRIDIH2 AS, focusing on hydrogen production and energy systems, and PISCI AS, focusing on sustainable Arctic-char farming. Together they form a cohesive, technology-driven platform for circular industrial development aligned with the European Green Deal and ESA initiatives for sustainable, data-integrated resource systems.
NAPOP’s technologies and data-driven integration model align closely with ESA’s priorities for sustainability, resilience, and digitalization of energy systems. Its operations use Earth-Observation (EO) and satellite-navigation (SatNav) data for site evaluation and optimization of renewable-energy potential, environmental and water-quality monitoring in aquaculture, and dynamic energy management where real-time EO, IoT, and grid data support predictive control and system resilience. These capabilities position NAPOP as a relevant downstream use case within ESA’s Earth Observation for Green Transition and Energy & Environment programmes, demonstrating how space-based data can optimize circular, low-carbon industrial ecosystems on Earth.

entityDescription:
Company OverviewUncharted AI is a deep-tech robotics and artificial intelligence company pioneering autonomous systems for planetary exploration and in-situ resource utilization (ISRU). Originating from research at Polytechnique Montréal’s MIST Lab, Uncharted AI combines multi-robot autonomy, advanced perception, and AI-driven geological intelligence to enable sustainable exploration and extraction of space resources.
Core ExpertiseOur technologies bridge autonomy, sensing, and analytics for robotic operations in GPS-denied, communication-limited, and unstructured environments. We design and deploy AI-powered robotic platforms capable of autonomous exploration, mapping, excavation, and processing of extraterrestrial regolith.Key capabilities include:• Risk-aware multi-robot exploration and mapping for complex terrains such as craters, lava tubes, and regolith fields.• Autonomous excavation and beneficiation of lunar and Martian soil using robotic manipulators and onboard analytical instruments.• Multi-sensor fusion frameworks integrating LiDAR, hyperspectral, GPR, and thermal sensing for sub-surface characterization.• Digital twin and mission planning software for closed-loop control between Earth-based operators and autonomous agents.
Space ApplicationsUncharted AI’s developments directly address challenges in space mining and ISRU operations, including prospecting, excavation, beneficiation, and material handling in lunar and Martian environments.Our robotic systems autonomously identify high-value mineral or volatile-rich zones, perform in-situ processing, and generate actionable insights for science and engineering missions.
Experience and CollaborationsUncharted AI participated in the European Space Agency (ESA) – ESRIC Space Resources Challenge, demonstrating an end-to-end autonomous beneficiation system at the DLR LUNA analog lunar environment in Cologne, Germany.We collaborate with academic institutions, research centers, and industrial partners across Europe and Canada to develop next-generation robotic systems for planetary operations, defense, and extreme-environment exploration.
Mission StatementAt Uncharted AI, we envision a future where intelligent robotic systems extend human capability beyond Earth, enabling responsible and scalable utilization of extraterrestrial resources. Our mission is to make space mining autonomous, sustainable, and data-driven—transforming planetary exploration into a self-reliant, science-enabled industry.

entityDescription:
Spaider Srl develops AI-driven software solutions for engineering simulation and design acceleration, enabling real-time prediction and optimization of complex physical systems. By combining deep learning with physics-based models, Spaider reduces computational time and costs by up to 70% compared to traditional numerical simulation methods (CFD, FEM, multiphysics).
Its technology supports aerospace, automotive, energy, and electronics industries by integrating seamlessly with existing digital engineering workflows. Spaider’s AI networks learn from historical simulation data to create self-improving predictive models, preserving engineering know-how and enhancing design efficiency.
In the space sector, Spaider’s applications include thermal management of spacecraft components, aerothermodynamics of re-entry vehicles, drag estimation in VLEO, combustion chamber and nozzle cooling modelling, supporting faster and more cost-effective development of next-generation systems.
